title: ES6+ syntax: let/const, arrow functions and template strings

videos.script:
JavaScript runs in two places in this course. {{two}} One is the browser, where it was born, and where every page you open runs some of it. The other is Node.js, which takes the same language out of the browser and runs it on a computer like any other program.

By the end of today you will have both working. {{lab}} First you set up your own computer: Node, and a small program called page that opens a page in a real browser and prints what it said. Then you run a file with node, open a page with page, and see the same line print in each.

Then three pieces of syntax you will type every day. {{let}} let and const, which say whether a name may be pointed somewhere else later. {{arrow}} Arrow functions, the short way to write a function, with one trap you will meet in the first week. {{template}} And template strings, the backticks, which put values inside text without a single plus sign.

This is the syntax people call ES6, after the 2015 edition of the standard that brought most of it in. Ten years on, it is simply JavaScript. Anything older that you find online, you will be able to read, but you will not need to write it.

One more thing before you start. {{fails}} Installing a language is where many people give up, so one section is about what to do when it fails. Read it before you need it.
